newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Littoral sees Lufthansa deal boosting sales. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Air Littoral sees Lufthansa deal boosting sales. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]

text.p: French regional airline Air Littoral said a marketing and ticket code-sharing agreement signed with Lufthansa on Thursday would boost sales by between 20-25 percent a year once the deal was fully operational.

Air Littoral chairman Marc (corrects from Henri) Dufour told a news conference that consolidated turnover for the 1997/98 year would be around 1.5 billion francs and net profit would be about 30 million.

"In a full year we expect sales growth of between 20-25 percent thanks to this agreement. Profit growth will be between 10-15 percent," he told Reuters after a news conference to announce the marketing pact.
"Profit growth will be small because there will be investment for development and we put the priority on growth," Dufour said.

Air Littoral, majority-owned by French businessman Michel Seydoux, earlier signed a wide-ranging marketing and technical agreement with Lufthansa aimed at extending their route and ticket sales networks.
As part of the cooperation pact, Air Littoral plans to issue eight-year convertible bonds to Lufthansa which will allow the German company to buy up to 15 percent of the French firm's capital.
The bond issue "will be done quickly", Dufour told Reuters.
